name: British Kings and Queens
description: Every king and queen of England and Great Britain, from Alfred the Great to Charles III, with the year each one took the throne.

checkpoints.name: Anglo-Saxons and Danes
checkpoints.note: Alfred the Great holds Wessex against the Vikings and his grandson Æthelstan becomes the first king of all England. The Danish king Cnut rules from 1016, and the old royal line returns with Edward the Confessor.

checkpoints.name: Normans
checkpoints.note: William of Normandy wins the crown at Hastings in 1066. His sons William II and Henry I follow, and then Stephen, whose reign is torn by civil war.

checkpoints.name: Plantagenets
checkpoints.note: Henry II founds a line that rules for more than two centuries. It includes Richard the Lionheart, John and Magna Carta, the three Edwards and the long war with France.

checkpoints.name: Lancaster and York
checkpoints.note: Henry IV takes the throne from Richard II. Two branches of the royal family then fight for it in the Wars of the Roses.

checkpoints.name: Tudors
checkpoints.note: Henry VII wins the crown at Bosworth. His son Henry VIII breaks with Rome, and Elizabeth I reigns for forty-four years.

checkpoints.name: Stuarts
checkpoints.note: James VI of Scotland inherits the English throne. The century brings civil war, the execution of Charles I, a republic under Cromwell, the Restoration and, in 1707, the union of England and Scotland.

checkpoints.name: Hanoverians
checkpoints.note: George I arrives from Hanover in 1714. The line runs through four Georges and William IV to Victoria, who reigns for sixty-three years.

checkpoints.name: Windsors
checkpoints.note: Edward VII opens the twentieth century. The family takes the name Windsor in 1917, and Elizabeth II reigns for seventy years before Charles III.
